data.name: Alaric
data.gender_notes: Alaric is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Germanic elements al (all) and ric (ruler or power). Alaric translates to 'ruler of all'. This name was borne by several early Germanic kings, most notably Alaric I, who ruled the Visigoths from 409 to 410 AD and sacked Rome. The name Alaric carries the meaning “Ruler or protector” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alaric usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler or protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to use one's power and leadership for the greater good.
data.etymology: Alaric belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler or protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alaric total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Alaric
in_english.meaning: Germanic name with meaning of courage and strength
in_english.long_meaning: the name Alaric is of Germanic origin, derived from the Gothic words 'Als' and 'Rik' meaning 'brave' or 'leader', in Christian context, the name Alaric symbolizes courage and boldness, and is commonly used among Christians in Europe

data.cultural_impact: Alaric is most significantly known as the leader who sacked Rome in 410 AD, marking the end of ancient Rome's glory and the beginning of the Middle Ages. His name became synonymous with the fall of the Roman Empire and the shift in political and cultural power from antiquity to the Middle Ages.
data.spiritual_significance: Alaric's name has spiritual significance as it embodies the idea of a ruler invested with divine power and authority to govern all. In Christian mythology, Alaric is portrayed as a devout king who sought the guidance and protection of Saint Martin of Tours, demonstrating the importance of faith and divine intervention in leadership. Alaric's legacy serves as a reminder that power and authority are not just worldly achievements, but also spiritual callings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Alaric, meaning "ruler of all," embodies the spiritual journey of a strong and wise leader, guiding his people towards the light of God's kingdom. In times of hardship and challenge, Alaric's name echoes the promise of divine protection and the ability to rule with compassion, justice, and faith.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Alaric I sacked Rome in 410 CE The name Alaric carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Alaric remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Thomas Alaric from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Alaric - "Ruler or protector". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
